utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon everyone again. Mr. Tolimir, I'd like to confirm that you are receiving interpretation into a language that you understand. I see that you are nodding. And should you have any difficulties -- if you have any difficulties with the -- that, please let me know as we're proceeding. May I have -- well, I note the appearances for the Prosecution, Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Chris Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: And Mr. Mitchell. Thank you. And Mr. Tolimir I note is here, and I understand as well, Mr. Tolimir, you have with you today your case manager. Sir, could you introduce yourself please for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEKULIC
utterances.text: Assisting Mr. Tolimir in court today, Vuk Sekulic attorney-at-law from Belgrade and case manager for General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much and welcome, sir. All right. This is the third Status Conference for -- for this case, and pursuant to Rule 65 bis (A), the purpose is of course to have, exchanges between the parties to ensure an expeditious preparation of the trial and also to review the status of the case and to deal with any issues including issues relating to the circumstances of the accused. I have essentially two items only for today's proceedings. I am aware, Mr. Tolimir, of your filing which I received on the 19th of February. You filed it on the 13th. And I will, of course, also ask the Prosecutor if they have any matters to raise, and then there are the regular matters we'll deal with at the end. It is my understanding we only have a very limited amount of time today because it's a busy day for Status Conferences, so I would ask everyone if we can keep our submissions short and focused so that we can complete things within the scheduled time. I'm going to deal first of all with -- with the issue of the confidentiality order, Mr. Tolimir, that I issued on the 28th of February. Now, normally issues of this nature relating to disclosure, confidential materials are matters that are dealt with as between counsel for the Prosecution and counsel for the Defence, but obviously in a case such as this of a self-represented accused, that is not possible and that is the reason for the intervention of the Pre-Trial Judge in this instance. On the 28th of February I issued an order for the protection of confidentiality of disclosed materials and because of the importance of this issue, Mr. Tolimir, and in particular in light of my obligation under Article 20 of the Statute to always have due regard to the protection of victims and witnesses, I want to review the nature and content of this order with you this afternoon to make sure that you understand it. Amongst the material the Prosecution may disclose to you or you may otherwise receive will be statements, testimony given by individuals who have been accorded protective measures by this Tribunal. These kinds of measures can take different forms. For example, the name of the person might be protected from public disclosure and he or she may be assigned a pseudonym, and in court even we go to the -- we use on occasion measures of preventing the public from seeing or hearing the witness in their normal voice or normal appearance. And in addition sometimes evidence is taken in a private or a closed session, which means it cannot be disclosed to the public. So in those cases, Mr. Tolimir, when you receive material of this nature, you are precluded from disclosing such information to anyone other than, of course, members of your legal team which will have access to that material but are similarly bound not to disclose or disseminate the identifying information about a witness or about what was said in closed or private session. To do so, of course, would violate the protective order issued by the Tribunal. In addition, Mr. Tolimir, you may receive material which is marked as confidential. For example, the Prosecution might have been provided with documentation by a country, by an individual, but on a condition that it not be disclosed publicly. And here again, that material must be kept confidential by you and your legal team. The same is true of motions that may be filed confidentially or even decisions issued by the Tribunal confidentially. This order that I issued on the 28th obligates you to keep all of that kind of material confidential. If an issue arises, of course, as to the basis upon which perhaps the Prosecution is alleging that material is confidential and you challenge that, you can certainly bring that to the attention of the Trial Chamber. But insofar as and in the absence of a ruling to the contrary, if the material is marked as confidential, then it must be treated and respected as such. Do you understand this, Mr. Tolimir? Have I -- have I made this clear?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would like to greet you and the gentlemen, and I would like to bring this trial to an end with faith in God and as -- and God's will may be served, and now let us pay respect to the late Nebojsa Mrksic who represented me in this case for five months. He died 12 days ago and he's a member of the lawyer's Chamber of this court so I would like to pay respect by one minute of silence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. We were aware of the very sad death of Mr. Mrksic and the Trial Chamber in the Popovic et al. Trial has offered our condolences to his family. So thank you for that. And I take it from your comments you do understand the explanation that I have provided regarding the confidentiality of material. Is that correct, Mr. Tolimir? Could you confirm that for me please, on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will answer your question now before I move on to the issues that I would like to raise. I would like to inform you that I am not aware of anything. Nothing has been disclosed to me, not even the enlarged indictment, amended indictment. So I cannot commit any breaches on confidentiality, and I would also like to inform you that nothing is being disclosed to me in a language that I understand with regard to the submissions and motions by the Chamber. So there's nothing I can disclose to the public. I would also like to tell you that I am not able to read the electronic mail. I don't have a computer. So there's nothing I can disclose to the public. And thirdly, thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. We will come to the issues that you've raised, because the next issue I'm going to deal with is in direct response to the issues that you have just noted. I simply wanted to confirm, and I am satisfied by your response that you understand the nature of the confidentiality order, and I'm assuming that you will respect it. So I'm satisfied that you are now aware, whether you've received it in writing or not, you are aware from the oral comments I have made that that order is in place and of the obligations under the Statute generally. Now, I'm going to move to my second issue which, Mr. Tolimir, will also deal with a number of the issues that you have indicated you wished to discuss today. It seems evident to me, Mr. Tolimir, from looking at your filings and from hearing your submissions that there is some clarification needed here as to the court process. Not just the court process here but it is a general process in most courts that I am aware of. While you have the right, Mr. Tolimir, albeit not an unqualified one, to elect self-representation, you do not have the right to elect the procedure that will be followed in this Tribunal. As I explained to you when we met previously and you indicated your intent to represent yourself, you are responsible to present your case in accordance with the procedure as defined by the Statute, the Rules, and the jurisprudence. Now, in accordance with that procedure, both parties, both you and the Prosecution, are entitled to bring issues before me and before the Trial Chamber. And provided those are matters properly before us, once they are raised both parties are given an opportunity to address the issues, orally in some instances but in many instances in writing as well, and within specified time limits. On occasion as well, we may ask for or the Registrar may make submissions on those issues. After this, after the submissions are made, I as the Pre-Trial Judge or the Trial Chamber will render a decision. Once that decision is made, Mr. Tolimir, once it is rendered and issued, that is the end of the matter. It is not open to the parties, to either party, to continually reargue the issue, to continue to make submissions which are directly contrary to the decision or to continually return to the same point. You can, of course, seek clarification of a decision if something is not clear, or in a very, very exceptional circumstance you might formally seek reconsideration but this would be a rare occasion and you would have to do it formally in writing. In essence, the principle, Mr. Tolimir, which applies in all courts and legal systems, once a decision is made it is final and the issue ends there. The exception, of course, is if you wish to appeal my decision or a decision of the Trial Chamber. In most instances in this Tribunal that will require the certification of the decision by the Trial Chamber. But if that is given, then you may bring the matter to the Appeals Chamber, and you may reargue it before the Appeals Chamber. Such requests and appeals, however, are to be brought within specified time limits as well. And even in that circumstance where you bring a matter to the Appeals Chamber, until and unless the Appeals Chamber issues a decision to the contrary, overturns the position taken by the Trial Chamber or by me, our rulings stand and there is no opportunity to rearguing the same issue either in writing or orally. In -- in this case one of the issues, and I'll touch on two others that you've raised today, but one of the issues which you continue to raise, Mr. Tolimir, and you have again today, is the language of communication. Now, as you know, on December 11th of 2007 I issued a ruling on that matter. You requested on the 17th of December certification of my decision, and on the 15th of January, the Trial Chamber granted you certification and that matter you have now brought before the Appeals Chamber and it is pending there. And I would also note, Mr. Tolimir, because this is apparently not clear to you, on the same day, the 15th of January, the Trial Chamber rendered another decision on your written submission of 7th December on the same issue, the language issue, and we denied your motion but we also granted you certification of that written decision so you could raise it in conjunction with the appeal of the oral decision. However, as I say, that's where the matter stands. The matter is pending before the Appeals Chamber, and we are not going to deal with the language issue further, neither here nor in terms of written material that you may file. So I am aware of your filings of the 25th of January, submitted on the 23rd; of the 5th of February submitted by you on the 31st of January; and a second one on the 5th of February which was submitted by you on the 1st of February, but they will not be addressed by the Trial Chamber nor by me, and it is in fact within the discretion of the Registrar to refuse in future to accept filings on this subject because they are not properly before the Tribunal. All of this, I emphasise, is subject to, of course, the Appeals Chamber's decision. If they take a decision to the contrary, then we're going to have to review a number of matters, but we will only revisit it if and when that becomes necessary as a result of an Appeals Chamber ruling. So I hope that is clear to you Mr. Tolimir. In addition, when I look at the agenda items you put forward for today, most of them are subject to the same difficulty in that they relate to matters already decided by the Trial Chamber. I'll take each one in turn, but you need to understand I'm not entertaining submissions on issues already decided by me or by the Trial Chamber. So I turn to the matters you have raised, the four issues. I begin with the last one which I need say no more on. It's a question of the language of communication. As indicated, that matter has been ruled on and we will discuss it no further. The first agenda item you have proposed is a discussion related to your alleged kidnapping and the resolution of related issues of status. That issue, Mr. Tolimir, has been raised by you previously, argued by you on a couple of occasions orally, and you also made written submissions to the Trial Chamber in your Rule 72 motion filed on the 7th of November, 2007. You chose to do so. The Trial Chamber has ruled on that matter, Mr. Tolimir, in its decision on preliminary motions on the indictment pursuant to Rule 72 issued on the 14th of December. I don't know if you've read that decision, but I can assure you that within that decision the Trial Chamber dealt with your arguments as well as the submissions of the Prosecution and ruled on the question of your circumstances of arrest and its impact or not on your -- on the jurisdiction. As the matter has been decided, I will not hear further submissions on it today. The only caveat to that, Mr. Tolimir, because this is a particularly sensitive issue, is if, and I stress if, you have obtained new evidence. Not information, not rumours, not simply that you have new arguments to take. If you have new evidence that fundamentally changes the factual basis for the Trial Chamber's ruling then you may bring that to our attention for consideration, but it must be done so in writing, and it must include the actual evidence that you're referring to. But otherwise, we will discuss the matter no further today. And finally, as for the second issue that you raised, this is the failure, as you titled it, the failure of the Prosecution to disclose under Rule 66(A)(i). This again is a matter that has been concluded. Based on the information before me on July 3rd of 2007, I found the Prosecution had met its disclosure obligations. However, at that time, the time limits for your Rule 72 motions normally would have run. I, however, stayed them at that time. I did not require you in July to file your preliminary motions because there was still an issue of the appointment of counsel. Once you decided that you were going to represent yourself, I then, as we discussed and I did this at a Status Conference, I set filing deadlines for the Rule 72 motion, and I explained to you what those motions were and that they needed to be filed, and in fact you filed a Rule 72 motion on the 7th of November as we've just discussed. Therefore, in terms of Rule 66(A)(i), and this is distinct from 66(A)(ii) where there is still ongoing disclosure matters, that is a closed issue as is the preliminary motion under Rule 72. So therefore the issue that we are left with, Mr. Tolimir, for this afternoon amongst the issues that you have raised is that relating to the appointment of your -- as I take it an individual you would like appointed as a legal advisor on international law. It is the third issue that you have raised. In raising that point you have also highlighted some issues you're having with the Registrar about communications and faxes and things of that nature. I don't think we need to discuss that issue today, Mr. Tolimir, because from reading the material from you and from the Registrar, it's apparent to me that's just a procedural matter and that there is no issue there that requires intervention from the Trial Chamber. However, I have looked very carefully, Mr. Tolimir, at the issue you've identified relating to Mr. Gajic, and I have reviewed that as well as the Registrar's response, but I will give you an opportunity now to speak to that issue. I am concerned about the point you have raised, Mr. Tolimir, and you can take it for granted I have read the submissions, but I invite you at this point if you wish to make any further submissions on that question, the appointment of Mr. Gajic, if you could do that at this time, please, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think that you want me not to raise the issues that are supposed to resolve the further procedure here and the pre-trial stage of this trial, and if you don't want me to speak about them, then I don't want to speak about them, but I would like to warn you that this is similar situation to two people playing chess, one of them not being aware of the rules and the other one being a good player. I can't play chess with you because I can't play, and you on the other hand are good chess players. I haven't received anything not even the amended indictment. But if you don't want me to speak, I won't speak. But I would like to offer you a solution to the problem and I would like to state for the record that I have not received anything save for the indictment that was brought to me to my hospital bed after the arrest. I have not received the amended indictment or any material and you know it. And you issued a ruling, although we told you at the Status Conference that nothing has been disclosed to me. You were told that by the Prosecutor and by myself. If you made your decision fully aware that no disclosure has taken place, I'm sure that you can change your ruling or that you can find a solution that would not block the work of the Prosecution. You are not preventing me for -- from representing myself but you are blocking the work of the Prosecution. If you want to transfer my rights onto the Prosecution, I won't prevent you in doing that. I don't want you to impose a language that I'm going to use upon me. This is not an issue that I'm going to talk about that but this is not a criterion that leads to a just and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir. Mr. Tolimir, I think I've made myself very clear. It's not a question of the substance of the issue. That issue is before the Appeals Chamber at the moment. So -- but what I am offering you an opportunity to do, you have raised an issue that I take it -- you've raised it very clearly that I take it is of concern to you which is the appointment of Mr. Gajic. And I would like to hear from you because I take it as a very serious matter, the composition of the team that will assist you with your defence. So I would like to hear from you right now is on that, if you have anything further. I have taken your comments into account and I find them quite persuasive, Mr. Tolimir, on the issue of his appointment. So please could you address me on that issue. I'm interested in hearing from you on that point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I just wanted to offer two remarks on the things that you already shared with us because I was the one who called this Status Conference and I would kindly ask you to allow me to offer these two remarks. Don't forbid me to do that. I would just like to state for the record that you are forbidding me to talk about the problems and issues that would lead to a fair trial. I would just like to say that you are preventing me from talking about my kidnapping and my remark on that ban of yours is this: The document you are talking about and here that you discussed and that you used to resolve the problem of kidnapping, I never received that. And you said it yourself at the last Status Conference, if the accused does not receive a document in a language that he can understand, it will be construed as the document has not been received. Also, if a document is sent by the accused, is sent to the Pre-Trial Chamber it will be considered as not received if it hasn't been translated into the language that the Trial Chamber understands. I'm just trying to share with you those things that I find important with regard to the kidnapping which would be a new fact for you. If you want to render a new ruling, please allow me to say something. If not, then I will obviously comply with your ruling, but please allow me the right that I am supposed to have. If you allow me, I will offer just one fact about the kidnapping. If you don't allow me to do that then I will comply with your decision obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, as I indicated, if you have new evidence relating to the kidnapping, then I would suggest that you bring that forward to me. You're quite capable of making submissions, so I would suggest that you bring that forward in writing, because it would have to be a sufficiently important factual matter that the Trial Chamber would want to see it in writing in order to reconsider a decision that it has taken. So I gave you the caveat with respect to a decision that's already been made that if you have new factual information, I am inviting you by way of a submission to make that apparent to the Trial Chamber for the Trial Chamber's consideration. But in the case of a reconsideration, it's not something that you're simply going to be allowed to reargue orally without us knowing whether or not there is any basis for us to reconsider. So that's the reason why. If you have new factual evidence related to that issue, because it is an issue we have already determined, then please bring it forward in writing to the Trial Chamber so we can assess if there is any basis for reconsideration and solely because of the jurisdictional nature of that issue. So I'd like to leave that issue for today, but again, and I'll try one more time, otherwise I'm simply going to have to base it on what you have said in your written submissions which are, as I say, quite persuasive but I would like you to address the appointment of your legal advisor or second legal advisor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. After just one sentence related to this note that I made that I have not been made aware of any of your decisions. I just want to note that at one Status Conference you gave the Prosecutor the mandate to investigate the kidnapping. I'm not going to go into this in any detail, but the Prosecution never informed me of the results of the investigation, and the Trial Chamber has not informed me about that. You have to inform me about that either in writing in a language that I understand or orally, but let me just share one fact with you. In the course of the investigation the Prosecution could do something, and if you want to allow me to say just one sentence, then please do so unless you think that the building will fall down about our ears if I do so. So do you allow me to say just one sentence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, my point is we're not going to spend time today revisiting issues that have already been decided by the Trial Chamber or by myself as a Pre-Trial Judge. So this is an issue which has already been decided. I have given you an opportunity in terms of submitting written material which is -- which is exceptional, I stress that, it's exceptional that I would even allow you to make the submissions on an issue that's already been decided by the entire Trial Chamber. So, no, we're not going to discuss that issue today. I have made my position clear. But again, could we move, please, to the issue of the appointment of your legal advisor, and I will hear you on that. It is an issue that I have not -- has not been dealt with by the Pre-Trial Judge or by the Chamber. So please, could we move to the issue of the appointment of the legal advisor and any additional points you wanted to make to me on that issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me just tell you that I don't want to discuss the kidnapping but I'm just letting you know that I have taken measures outside of this court because you're not allowing me to do so within the court to institute criminal proceedings against Boris Tadic, the president of the present Tribunal Mr. Pocar, Chief Prosecutor Carla Del Ponte, and Mr. McCloskey who is in charge of this investigation before this court. I will file a legal suit before the International Court of Justice, because they are covering up the fact that I was kidnapped in Serbia and transferred to Bosnia and Herzegovina, and because this Tribunal wants to refer my case to Sarajevo, and this is why I'm forced to use B/C/S, the language that was invented after the war. And I will, I will pursue with this legal suit because I have evidence for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, do you wish to say anything to me regarding the appointment of your legal advisor? And I'm taking it from your refusal to do so that you have nothing further to add on this issue; is that correct? On the issue of the appointment of your legal advisor, you have nothing further other than what you submitted to me in your submission; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is not correct. I have several things to tell you. The pre-trial period lasts for ten months and my legal advisors have yet to be appointed. I have filed a request for the appointment of three legal advisors and only one legal advisor has been appointed so far. The other persons are appointed to some other positions in accordance with the wishes of the Prosecution, and I don't like that. I informed you about that when I wrote a submission regarding Aleksandar Gajic, my advisor for international law and at the moment when I need him most for my legal suit regarding the illegal kidnapping. So I would like you to issue a decision appointing Mr. Gajic since he is an associate member of the bar association here at the Tribunal, and he meets all the requirements, although he doesn't have to because I selected him and he's my advisor, not your advisor. He represents me. And I would just like to add something on the issue of the appointment of my legal advisors. You have to assist me because I asked for your assistance in this. You have to exert pressure for my legal advisors to be appointed and for my legal team to be established because the legal advisors that I select are being rejected, and they're being appointed to some other positions, and my authentic desires are not being complied with. And I would also like to inform you that I'm not allowed to contact even this member of my team, Mr. Vuk Sekulic. So I have only private contacts with him, and I don't think it's proper. And the Registry wants to be in contact with him and to send documents to him. So I would just like to inform you, and I would like that to be reflected in the record. All the documents that are served on any members of my Defence team are considered to be not valid and not received by me, because I never received them. And the Registry cannot serve my documents to my team and my legal advisors and then they are supposed to give me advice on something that I myself have not read. This is impossible, untenable. So I would like to urge you to consider the time frame for the appointment of members of my legal team in this case. I'm not talking about what you've already decided upon, but the Registry has decided that my legal advisors may work only 100 hours a month and the rate is 25 euros. And this has put me at a disadvantage in relation to other accused before this Tribunal, because the other accused in this Tribunal have four times as much time for their defence in the pre-trial period, and the rate is four times as high, and this is a clear violation of Rules 20 and 21 on the equality of arms before this Tribunal. And in some cases, and you have the jurisprudence at your disposal, I don't because it has not been given to me despite my demands to have it, in cases that are at a low level -- lower level than mine, 3 million euros were spent in the pre-trial period, and I am given 80.000 euros for the pre-trial period. Ten months have passed and I have yet to see a single document in the pre-trial stage. So how can I be at an equal footing? I am at a disadvantage. I'm prejudiced here. And I have to now waive my rights to have documents in my mother tongue. And I can only defend myself in a language that is part of my genetic inheritance. Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I'll stop you there because you're reverting to an issue that we're not going to cover today but you have focused, thank you, on the issue that I wished to hear from you on which is, in particular, the appointment of your third team member. Now, let me make one preliminary comment just in relation to the last comments you were making. You will recall, Mr. Tolimir, because we went through this very carefully, by virtue of your election to represent yourself and by virtue of the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, in particular the Appeals Chamber decision in Krajisnik there will be differences indeed for the amount of time and the amount of payment available, because what you have in place are a team of individuals of different capacities who will assist you in representing yourself. What other accused have in place in many instances is Defence counsel who are defending them. So it's not useful for us to go through comparisons on that point today nor, as I say, do we need to discuss the communication issue because from reading the Registrar's submissions there is no issue there. It's clearly just a procedural matter. However, I have taken on board the comments you have made regarding Mr. Gajic. In particular, what you are saying is that you wish him to be one of the four members of your team who would be paid for out of the funds here, and you would like him to have the role as an advisor on international law. And I understand that wish on your part, and I find your comments that he should be appointed in the capacity as a legal advisor in that context to be quite persuasive. So what I'm going to do, Mr. Tolimir -- now, you have already in place, as we can tell today, your case manager, and you also have Mr. Milovancevic in place as a legal advisor. So we are certainly making progress in terms of the appointment of your team. I am going to invite the Registry to reconsider and revisit the issue of the appointment of Mr. Gajic. I'm going to ask them and encourage them to find a solution. I understand that they're concerned about the application of a policy in a neutral way in terms of all accused representing themselves. I understand the various concerns they have to balance, but I'm going to invite them and encourage them to find a solution that will allow him to be appointed pursuant to your wishes as a -- in a legal capacity which is the role that you wish him to fulfil. So I have indicated that on the record, and it will be communicated to the Registrar. And what I would say is I would ask them to do so in a timely fashion, as urgently as possible to look at the issue, and if you could continue to discuss the matter with them. And if within a reasonable period of time the issue still remains outstanding and has not been dealt with, then you can bring the matter back to me and at that time the Trial Chamber will look at it in terms of making an actual ruling. So hopefully, Mr. Tolimir, that will assist you with that particular issue of the constitution of your Defence team. I want to move on, then, to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Your Honour, we actually have a comment on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir, but, as I say, only on the issues I have identified.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the accused. Microphone -- 9

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Sir, you have to turn your microphone on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last sentence in what you've just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: You'd like me to repeat that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I would like to ask you something in relation to this sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I don't know to what extent the Registry is competent or not in light of the fact I've been left without my legal advisors for the ten months of the pre-trial proceedings. The legal assistance that I am entitled to under Article 21, 4, D of the Statute, and I want to know whether it is in line with the principle of beyond reasonable -- of proving beyond reasonable doubt for me to be left without a legal team for the ten months of the pre-trial proceedings, whether it is up to the standard of reasonable doubt, because I am greatly prejudiced by this. I cannot take certain procedural measures and actions by dint of the fact that I don't have a legal team, and I actually don't have the pre-trial stage to do those things. So could you please deal with that, because I don't know what the competencies are of the Registry or of the Court. If I am to be tried by the Registry, I have to also say that I feel like a prisoner of war because I was kidnapped. I would like you to transfer me to the jurisdiction of the military court of NATO, because I never received any paper, not even the amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, as I think I have you've explained to you on previous occasions, the Registrar has the primary responsibility for matters relating to the appointment of your assistants, your team, for your defence. I would note that this is being done on the basis of funding by the Tribunal, which is the reason that the Registrar has the role that it does with respect to these appointments, and they have a responsibility when they're dealing with the public funds to ensure that it is done properly and in accordance with the proper procedure and that it reflects an appropriate scenario for the appointment, publicly funded appointment, of the members of your team. I am quite confident that the Registrar from all the materials filed has been doing a very diligent job in trying to arrange for the appointment of your Defence team. So we're going to leave the matter in the hands, the very competent hands of the Registrar. You are certainly open to continue to discuss the matter with him. The Chamber is not issuing any ruling at this stage as I've said but I have made my hope very clear to the Registrar that there will be an early resolution of the issue of the appointment of Mr. Gajic. So we're going to leave that matter for today. You've made your comments clear on the record. And as we have very little time left we're going to proceed to a couple of other issues that we have to cover before the conclusion of today's Status Conference. But the matter has been addressed and I'm sure you will here from the Registrar on it. Now, I would like to turn -- Mr. McCloskey, I would assume that you did not have any comments on the particular issue of the appointment of the legal advisor. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: He's having trouble turning his microphone on. I've turned my off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. McCloskey, if we could turn to the issue of disclosure under -- and I stress, Mr. Tolimir, I'm now speaking to the Prosecution regarding disclosure under Rule 66(A)(ii), (ii), not the initial disclosure which triggers certain other responsibilities. But at the last occasion, the last Status Conference, Mr. McCloskey, we discussed the progress of that disclosure. Perhaps you could provide me with an update at this stage on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Certainly. We have now been to -- well, we have attempted to provide Mr. Tolimir with the witness list and the witness statements as provided by the Rule. Everything we have provided in hard copy has been returned, and we have been able to send material to his assistants, and the vast majority is now available to him via the EDS. They have passwords. They have the ability to do that. The -- one thing that is not yet available in terms of witness statements, as you know, there's additional statements coming out of the Popovic trial, and the only practical way of doing that is to provide audio, and the audiovisual people are doing that right now for the Popovic trial. They will be finished by the end of March they tell me, but we do have CDs and DVDs of the Krstic trial and the Blagojevic trial that are in a box that have gone back and forth at least once, and we -- there are a couple of other audio files of witnesses related to testimony in -- in other cases that we are tracking down but just a few. So we have met our obligation under that Rule except for those audio statements of the Popovic witnesses and, as you can imagine, most of those witnesses are on the witness list. Our witness list that we provided is 189 witnesses. Four of those are 92 quater witnesses, witnesses that have died that we will be providing under written statements. In the vast majority the rest of those witnesses will be provided -- offered under 92 bis for Mr. Tolimir. They will be provided -- or offered as written statements from their testimonies mostly. We have not made that final decision yet. But as for the requirements under Rule 66, we are almost there. The vast majority of the material is available to him through his team or we have the physical materials that we have any time they will be accepted. However, we have learned that his team does not have the authority to accept material, so we have not bothered them with that though we have provided them with all the e-mail information for EDS and we know that they -- Mr. Sekulic has worked here, is experienced, and has indicated to us that he knows all about how to use that and has a good reputation in the ICTY from what I gather. So it's available there, but how far it's gone beyond that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Tolimir, I don't, as I think I've made very clear, wish to return to the language issue or the service issue. However, what the Prosecution is outlining and information I have as well from the Registrar is that in addition to written material, you are being offered audiotapes, and there is also as well electronic material which can be played by your team if there's any issues regarding your ability to use the systems, in an electronic manner. So I am asking you to consider your acceptance of that material. I'm asking you to explain to me why you are not prepared to accept audio material which can be listened to, electronic material which can be viewed, particularly now that you have in place, as the Prosecution has just noted, a very competent case manager and as well you have a legal advisor, and hopefully you will have a team soon. So you do have a team to assist you and I fail to understand given the amount of material involved in this case, it is important to be able to use the electronic disclosure systems that are available. So if you have any particular comments you wish to make on that, on that specific issue of audio and electronic material, please, you can make those comments.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I carefully listened to what you and Mr. McCloskey had to say, and I would like you to consider what I am about to say and that it be recorded for the record. All the materials that Mr. McCloskey mentioned that are disclosed to my Defence team or to the case managers in my team are considered to be not valid and not received by me, and my Defence team has been informed about that, and Mr. McCloskey told you quite rightly that my team does not have the authority to receive those materials. So the first reason why I consider that I have not received the materials is because I do not understand the electronic form in which these documents are being served on me. Secondly, I want all the documents to be printed out in a language that I understand. I cannot, I cannot accept documents that are written in a language that I don't understand, and I cannot accept disclosure, written statements of the Prosecution witnesses and other materials, in a language that I don't understand because I cannot read those documents and I cannot question witnesses on something that I have not read. And I would like you to understand that my legal advisors cannot advise me about something that I have not read. How am I to say whether their advice is sound or unsound if I myself have not read the relevant documents? So I don't want you to put my Defence team in an unenviable position because they're not the team of the Registry or of the Chambers. They are my team. So I would like you to consider the issue of my communication with my team, with my legal advisors. I'm not allowed to communicate with my Defence team and my legal advisors. I am not allowed to do so by the Registry and I'm not allowed to send any written instructions to them. Yet Mr. McCloskey is sending tonnes of materials to them. It's an absurd situation and they're my legal advisors, my Defence team. So I would like this to be reflected in the record and you as a Judge to consider this issue whether the relevant jurisdictions of the Chambers and of the Registry and of the Prosecution as such, that they can contact my legal advisors, yet I cannot communicate with them. I asked the UN detention unit to allow me to give instructions to my legal team by phone. On the 4th of March I got approval to use this dedicated phone line, but with the proviso that I cannot give any written documents to my advisors and that they in turn receive all the documents for me from the Registry. They're not part of the Registry and of the Tribunal. They are only to be in contact with me. So I don't want to see this type of undermining of my Defence team, and I would like not to find myself in a situation where I cannot appoint people to posts that I want to appoint them to. I wanted to appoint Mr. Sekulic as my legal advisor yet the Registry appointed him the case manager so that he is the in-box for all the documents that are coming in. I want him to be my legal advisor as are Mr. Gajic and Mr. Milovancevic and yet this is not honoured. I would like you to bear that in mind and to deal with this and I would like this statement to be on the record. I hereby state for the record that I will be writing an appeal to the Tribunal's President against the decision of the Appeals Chamber should this decision dismiss my appeal and that the deadline for the appeal shall run from the date when I receive the decision of the Appeals Chamber in a language that I understand. I would like this to be reflected in the record given that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, thank you. Your statements are recorded on the record, but they are not responsive to the issue that I raised with you. As I mentioned, the issue of your communication and your ability to communicate with your legal team, with your team in general, is a matter that the Registrar has addressed very clearly in the submissions that they filed, and you can continue to discuss that matter with the Registry. I'm satisfied that the Registry is proceeding in accordance within appropriate procedure and at this stage there is nothing with respect to the communication issue that merits the intervention of the Trial Chamber or of me as the Pre-Trial Judge. So on the communication point that is a matter within the jurisdiction of the Registrar and at the moment there is not an issue for the Trial Chamber to consider. Now, secondly, as to the issue of the receipt of materials, you have not provided me with a satisfactory explanation as to why you are refusing to accept audio material which you could play and listen to yourself, nor in addition why you are not prepared to work with your own team in order to be able to benefit from the electronic materials that are being disclosed when you have a team that is competent in reviewing them and in discussing them with you. So what I'm going to do is I'm not going to take any decisions on this today. I'm going to ask you over the period -- the next period to consider your position in this regard, to consider whether you are prepared to work with the team that's been appointed to assist you in order that you can manage the massive amounts of material that have to be disclosed and considered in your case and some of which is coming to you in audio and electronic form which does not involve the language issue which is pending before the Appeals Chamber. So I'm going to ask you to consider that matter, and when we next meet we can see if matters have progressed at all in terms of your willingness to work with your team to -- in order to look at that material or listen to that material. So I'm going to leave that matter on that point today, and we will revisit the question of disclosure and the formats on another day. I'm going to proceed because we only have -- Mr. Tolimir, very briefly. We only have very few minutes left and there are some mandatory issues that we have to finish before we close. So very briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the most important thing in my view is to provide me with an ability to contact my legal team when I wanted and how I wanted. I inform you as a Pre-Trial Judge that I am being taken away even the submissions that I write in my own handwriting with an explanation that the detention unit cannot make any photocopies, and it is only at my specific request that I can receive these materials. I'm not raising any objections to your procedure. I just wanted to make it clear for the record that I don't even have the right to review the -- my own submissions. Sometimes when I write a submission to you, know, I don't know what was in it when I write my second submission. And as to your question, let me put it this way: In order for me to receive any video material I have to know what I am receiving and they are being disclosed to me in a language that I don't understand so I don't know what I am being disclosed. I would like to alert your attention to the fact that you should make a ruling for the detention unit to provide me with a room where there will be a fax machine, a telephone, a typewriter, a photocopier, and to be provided all this material because this material also falls under the fund, under the Rule 21(4)(b)[as interpreted] as minimal technical aid. All I have is a pencil. I don't have my own submissions. And I have live under such conditions for ten months, for the whole duration for the trial -- the pre-trial procedure. This is a game that both of us have been dragged into. You don't know that I have only a pencil. You are telling me that I have something else. I'm not a competent person to decide on that; somebody else is competent. I can bear that pressure but you just tell me this is in keeping with the rule of law with a fair trial or maybe this is a violation of all the rules of fair trial before this Tribunal. This is all I wanted to say and thank you very much for listening to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, you raised a number of these points in the submission that you made to me and I was cognisant of them, and the Registrar has filed a response submission addressing the points relating to communication. Now, you have chosen not to read that response. However, what I'm going to do is I'm going to ask the Registrar to go over with you again, as they have done, the circumstances surrounding your communications, because the information from the Registrar is certainly not that you are not entitled to have discussions with your team members. You are entitled with certain conditions to privileged discussions. You are entitled to access to communication equipment, et cetera. So that is a matter, however, what I have said, that falls within the Registrar's purview. It is the Registrar's primary area. We're going to close the discussion, Mr. Tolimir, but I am asking the Registrar to outline to you as they did in the written submission that they filed before the Trial Chamber the circumstances under which you can communicate and the issues that you have raised regarding your communications. And again if we reach a point where there is a particular issue at hand, then you can bring that matter back, but this is not a matter which the Trial Chamber or the Pre-Trial Judge is going to intervene in at this stage. You need to have this discussion again with the Registrar, and I'm asking the Registrar to go over those procedures with you again but we're going to have to close the subject for today. So we're going to move on at this time, Mr. Tolimir, just to the final point, which is -- we've already discussed the circumstances at the UNDU in terms of the conditions and the requests you're making regarding your work and those will be discussed with you by the Registrar, but are there any questions or issues you wish to bring to my attention regarding -- regarding your health, Mr. Tolimir? I will hear you, Mr. Tolimir, but not a continuation of the same debate over communications. As I say, that's matter you're going to have to take up with the Registrar, but go ahead if you have a question or issue you want to raise about your health or living conditions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I would just like to say that I have a written document that was read to me by the interpreter in the detention unit forbidding me to communicate with my legal advisor and forbidding me to photocopy my submissions with the remark that they are part of the case file. If you don't have that, I will make a copy of that and submit it to you. I don't have any communication with the Registry. You are the ones who should provide for that communication because the Registry writes in a language that I do not understand. Have you ever read any of my original submissions in the original language --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, if you have such a document, if you have a copy of that document that was read to you and you want to provide it to me, please do so. You may submit it and it will be brought to my attention. Okay? And I will look at that. I take it you have nothing in particular. Again, as always, I would give you the opportunity if you wish to go into private session but I take it you have nothing to raise regarding health issues at this time. Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me an opportunity to talk about my health. In the detention unit they took my blood pressure and they established the higher blood pressure is 120. The upper blood pressure HG and the lower is 75 HD, which means that it is even better than it is appropriate for my age. But I am being restricted in taking my teas. They don't allow me to drink tea. I am 74. I was operated for a kidney stone, and they don't allow me to drink Juva tea which I'm supposed to drink in order to excrete kidney stones. So could you please make sure I'm able to drink teas you can obtain in any shop or maybe the Registry should order the detention unit to either buy or order from a supply in Serbia or anywhere else this tea that I need to use. It doesn't really make sense for me not to be able to drink this very ordinary tea. Otherwise my health is good and I thank God for that and thank you for listening to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Well, that -- that request will be related to the Registry and hopefully that situation can be resolved as well. Thank you very much then. Mr. McCloskey, we have very limited time. Were there any other matters that the Prosecution wished to raise at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, I think then, Mr. Tolimir, that we're going to close the session for today. I would like you to think about the issues that we have talked about and about the disclosure matters, but our time is up for today, and therefore we will be adjourning the proceedings. I wish you a good afternoon to you and to everyone. Literally, Mr. Tolimir, we have one --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask you to call a Status Conference where you will give me more time to raise issues that are still pending in this case, the issues that you as the Pre-Trial Judge can deal with, because you're the one who deals with all the issues in dispute between the parties to the case. Nothing has been resolved, and it remains unresolved, and I wish to be treated as a prisoner of war and to be tried either by the Registry or a military court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Your comments are noted, Mr. Tolimir. Thank you. We stand adjourned.
